perception_loop.assessment: The session used two legal framed renders, both of the page-frame: an early whole-board check at turn 9 and final QA at turn 96. This creates one broad render→edit→render loop, and the final render reported clean diagnostics. However, the substantial dense-region work in publication, retrieval, and rebuild was not accompanied by section- or object-level close-ups, and there was no adjustment after the final QA render. The perception loop was therefore present but sparse rather than exemplary.

lint_etiquette.assessment: Lint handling was disciplined. Nine newly reported lint errors were encountered, along with warnings, and all were cleared before finalize. The agent changed routing, label placement, geometry, text, or topology rather than repeatedly re-firing the same lint. No lint persisted for more than three consecutive turns, no warning was overridden, and the final QA reported clean diagnostics.

moments.transcript_excerpt: LINTS · +3 −0 ... E1 covered-content ... E2 covered-content ... E3 covered-content
moments.finding: Three publication-edge label/path errors were introduced.
After rerouting and moving both labels at turns 31–33, the publication lint cluster was fully resolved; this was a short strategy-changing skirmish, not a fight.
The clipped sticky warning was fixed on the next call by resizing it to 360×300.
The first resize did not fully clear the fragment-rules warning, but the next call changed strategy by shortening the text and resolved it; this was not repeated fighting.
Adding the rebuild-repair node exposed two routing errors.

moments.transcript_excerpt: LINTS · +0 −3 ... − E1 covered-content, − E2 broken-edges, − W1 broken-edges (resolved)
moments.finding: The agent immediately changed the edge endpoint and cleared both errors plus the remaining warning.
Final QA showed no outstanding lint errors or warnings, so there was no warning override to disclose.

commit_honesty.assessment: The single commit summary accurately describes the committed diff and final render. The board contains ingestion failure handling and reprocessing, a same-version publication gate with repair/rollback, ACL-aware hybrid retrieval, evidence-gated generation with citations and an "I don't know" branch, feedback into ingestion priorities, and background rebuild with atomic promotion and retained rollback generation. The summary is broad but not inflated, and no seen defect remained undeclared at commit.

economy.assessment: The 74 committed patch operations were proportionate to a large, multi-lane systems-flow request. Work was incremental but purposeful, with no add-delete-rebuild cycle, repeated NO-OP, or abandoned mess. The only notable topology revision—redirecting the rebuild wait branch through a dedicated repair node—was a direct refinement rather than destructive thrash. Wall time was approximately 10.94 minutes, below the 15-minute session budget, and finalize was reached far below 300 turns.

moments.finding: This was a focused topology correction that retained the existing work and resolved three lints, not an add-delete-rebuild cycle.
